heading: Coming from Spring
body:
Tachyon uses plain English names (ADR 0047). So a reader who learned English as a second language can guess what each one does. This table maps each Spring name to its Tachyon name. It also shows what Tachyon leaves out on purpose. An annotation keeps the meaning of its Spring or Lombok counterpart, and Tachyon adds its own checks at build time. When you write a Spring name that has a Tachyon name, the build stops with TY1308 and names the new annotation. `ty migrate fix --write` renames these annotations for you, and it moves files into the new role folders, such as stores/, setups/, converters/ and delegates/. Older Tachyon names fail the same way: Client is now HTTPClient, WebCall is GetRequest and the other request annotations, TachyonTest is Test, and Resource is Needs. Behaviors is not an annotation at all: it is a name that Tachyon generates for its own code.

| Spring | Tachyon | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@SpringBootApplication` | No equivalent, by design | There is no main class to annotate. The folders and files define the project. Controllers live in server/controllers, views come from client/pages, and client/manifest.json declares what a document loads. |
| `@RestController` | @RequestRoute | Yon supports only REST, so every controller is a REST controller. It lives in server/controllers. |
| `@RequestMapping` | @RequestRoute | On the class, it gives the base path, such as @RequestRoute("/orders"). The compiler refuses RequestMapping and names RequestRoute. |
| `@PermitAll`, `permitAll()` | @Public | Anyone may call the route. Tachyon refuses a route that says nothing, like Spring Security when it denies by default. |
| `isAuthenticated()`, `@PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()")` | @SignedIn | Any signed-in user may call the route. |
| `@RolesAllowed`, `@Secured`, `hasRole(...)` | @Allow(Role) | Only a user with one of these roles may call the route. Roles are types, such as @Allow(Admin), not strings. |
| `AuthenticationProvider` | @IdentityProvider | The one class that reads the request and returns the user and their roles. Tachyon answers 401 or 403 before the method runs. |
| `@GetMapping, @PostMapping, @PutMapping, @PatchMapping, @DeleteMapping` | @GetRoute, @PostRoute, @PutRoute, @PatchRoute, @DeleteRoute | The method answers that verb at the class path plus its own path. Its name must start with the verb, such as getOrder. The server answers OPTIONS and HEAD. |
| `@RequestParam` | @FromQuery | On a controller argument, it reads one value from the query string (the part of the URL after ?). On a client, the Spring name RequestParam stays. |
| `@PathVariable` | @FromPath | On a controller argument, it reads a path variable, such as {id}. Its declared type is checked. On a client, the Spring name PathVariable stays. |
| `@RequestHeader`, `@CookieValue` | @FromHeader, @FromCookie | On a controller argument, they read one request header or one cookie. The build refuses CookieValue and names FromCookie. On a client, RequestHeader stays and sends the argument as a header. |
| `@RequestBody`, `@RequestPart` | @FromBody | On a controller argument, it reads the request body as JSON. A method has at most one, and a GET route has none. The build refuses RequestPart and names FromBody. On a client, RequestBody stays and sends the argument as the body. |
| `@HttpExchange`, `@GetExchange`, `@PostExchange`, `@PutExchange`, `@PatchExchange`, `@DeleteExchange` | @HTTPClient, @GetRequest, @PostRequest, @PutRequest, @PatchRequest, @DeleteRequest | A client is a contract with no implementation, like an HTTP service interface, in the realm's remotes folder. Tachyon writes the client from the Setup with the same stem. A method body, a field or a constructor fails the build with TY1308. |
| `@Autowired`, `@Inject`, `@Resource` | @Needs | Goes on a field that is not static and has no starting value. The provider comes from the field's declared type, or from its lowerCamel name in JavaScript. Only field injection exists. There is no constructor or setter form, except that an F# class takes its providers as primary constructor parameters. The field is never null, so the build refuses a nullable Needs field with TY1331. |
| `@RequiredArgsConstructor` (Lombok) | @NeedsAll | Every field without a starting value is required, as with Lombok. A field that holds a provider is injected, and every other required field comes from the component's props in Tac. NeedsAll takes no field list, and the class writes no constructor, because Tachyon writes it. |
| `@Scope` | @Lifetime | Yon takes one string: singleton, request or transient (Spring's prototype). Tac takes a literal object: {"value":"singleton"}, {"value":"prototype"} for one service per component, or {"value":"application"} for one service per app in a native macOS, Linux or Windows Rust app. |
| `@Qualifier` | @Named | Gives the provider's name directly, next to @Needs, when the field itself does not select one. If a name matches no provider in the entry scope, the build fails. |
| `@Service` | @Service | The same role, in the shared services folder of the realm. |
| `@Repository` | @Store | A Spring Data repository interface: a contract with no implementation that names its Entity. Each method is a derived query (a query built from the method name) or a Query, with size limits, and Tachyon writes it. Needs injects the store. |
| `CrudRepository<T, ID>` | Repository<Entity, Id> | The base of a Store: extending it gives `findById`, `findAll` (one page), `save` and `deleteById` without declaring them. Derived `deleteBy` methods remove every matching record and answer the count. |
| `@Component` | @Delegate | A class that services use for part of their work. It lives in client/delegates or server/delegates, and its name ends with Delegate. The name was Delegate before ADR 0112, and Component before that, because client/components holds views. A class with only static methods is a utility in utils instead. |
| `@Configuration` | @Setup | The same. It is the type that holds the configuration rules. It is a singleton too: Tachyon runs its configure method once per page in Tac and once per server process in Yon, and every client, store and service context built from it shares the same adapters. Each case of a test unit still starts with a fresh Setup, as if every test had `@DirtiesContext`. |
| `@Value` | @Setting | Puts one property into a field, with the ${name:default} syntax. |
| `@ConfigurationProperties` | @Settings | Binds the properties that share a prefix, such as {"prefix":"YON_CATALOG_"}, to the fields of a Setup or a Settings model in models/. Every key under the prefix must be a field. Tac reads only public TAC_ values. |
| `@Profile` | @WhenProfile | Uses the Setup only when one of the named profiles is on. |
| `@ConditionalOnProperty` | @WhenSetting | Uses the Setup only when a setting has a value. It keeps Spring's keys: name, havingValue and matchIfMissing. |
| `@PostConstruct`, `@PreDestroy` | @OnStart, @OnStop | The method runs once when the object starts or stops. A method has at most one of these hooks. |
| `@EventListener` | @OnEvent | The listener takes one model parameter, and that model's type is the event. Spring's list of event classes is not kept: write one method for each model. The options are condition, id and replay. A returned model is published as a new event. |
| `@Async` on a listener | @InBackground | Only on an OnEvent listener. The publisher does not wait. Yon accepts it in JavaScript, TypeScript and Python; Tac accepts it in every service language that has listeners. |
| `@Cacheable`, `@CachePut`, `@CacheEvict` | @Cached, @UpdateCache, @ClearCache | Cached keeps a method's answer for the same arguments. UpdateCache and ClearCache name the Cached method, such as {"method":"find"}, and run only after the method succeeds. A method has only one of the three. |
| `@CacheConfig` | @CacheSettings | Names the cache that the class's Cached methods use, and also sets its limits: ttlMs, maxBytes and maxEntries. Cached needs CacheSettings on its class. |
| `@PageableDefault` | @PageDefaults | Goes on the page parameter and gives the page size and sort order when the caller leaves them out. |
| `@Validated`, `@Valid` | @Checked, @Check | Checked marks the model in models/ whose fields are checked. Check goes on the method parameter and names that model. A check in Tac only helps the user; Yon must check the same data again. |
| `@NotNull`, `@NotBlank`, `@Size`, `@Min`, `@Max` | @Required, @NotEmpty, @Length, @Min, @Max | Field checks on a Checked model. Length takes {"min","max"}. |
| `@Bean` | The configure hook | A Setup gives named adapters from its configure method: caches, http, entities and the authorization hooks. There is no general bean container to add beans to. |
| `@Entity` | @Entity | Declares the adapter and the identifier that a Store uses. |
| `@Table` | @Table | The same. It names the table that an entity maps to. |
| `@Column` | Not supported | The field names of an entity are its column names. There is no way to rename a column. |
| `@Id` | @Id | Marks the identifier field. It must be the same field that @Entity declares. The compiler refuses a mismatch. |
| `@Mapper`, `@Mapping` (MapStruct) | @Converter, @Convert | This is not part of Spring Framework, but Spring applications often use this mapper. @Converter is the role, in converters/<Name>Converter, and it is a contract like a MapStruct interface: a method body fails the build with TY1308. Like a mapper bean, it needs no context, and a service or controller asks for it with @Needs. @Convert is the whole method. It is a fixed plan of fields, made of source paths with dots and constants, and it reads one JSON argument of limited size. There is no expression language, no `qualifiedByName` and no generated implementation class. The compiler writes the body itself. |
| `@Transactional` | @AllOrNothing | Goes on a service method and names the entity adapter that answers begin, commit and rollback. A store that the service injects joins the open transaction, like propagation REQUIRED. Every Store command inside the method is part of the transaction. There are no propagation modes and no savepoints. An inner one joins the open transaction. |
| `@TransactionalEventListener` | Not implemented | In the compiled languages, the event dispatcher and the behavior context share no handle (no shared reference). So a step that runs after the commit could work in only some Yon languages. Instead, publish the event after the transactional method returns. |
| `RemoteApplicationEvent` (Spring Cloud Bus) | `@Topic` on the model | A Topic model's events are saved in the topic log and reach the OnEvent listeners in the other Yon languages and in open pages, at most once. See Topics. |
| `@JsonComponent, @JsonMixin` | Not supported | The framework itself copies every value that crosses a boundary into JSON of limited size. An application serializer does not do this. There is no serializer registry to extend. |
| `@Lazy` | Already the behaviour | Tachyon creates a managed provider only when something asks for it. So the annotation would have nothing to turn on. |
| `@Retryable` | @Retry | The resilience annotation from Spring Framework 7, with millisecond literals instead of a TimeUnit: maxRetries, delayMs, multiplier, maxDelayMs and jitterMs. Tachyon never retries a framework refusal. |
| `@ConcurrencyLimit` | @MaxAtOnce | The same two policies, block and reject. A blocked caller waits only until its operation deadline. PHP accepts only reject. |
| `@Description` | @Description | One literal line of limited length that goes into the registration for tools to read. It goes on a class that already declares a behavior. |
| `@SpringBootTest` | @Test | A test unit is an entry. server/tests/<Name>Test.<ext> puts together the role files of its realm. The annotation names the Setup that its context comes from. Nothing is found automatically, so you name the Setup. |
| `@WebMvcTest`, `@DataJpaTest`, `@WebFluxTest`, `@JsonTest`, `@RestClientTest` | @Test | There is no shared container to divide into slices (smaller partial contexts). Each call owns its own set of instances, and you always select a Setup yourself. One annotation covers everything that the slices divided. |
| `@ParameterizedTest` with `@ValueSource` | @ValueSource | The test case lists its inputs; Tachyon runs one case for each input and passes it as the one argument. The case is found by its `test` name, so no `@ParameterizedTest` is needed. |
| `Assertions.assertEquals`, `assertTrue`, `assertThrows` | `Assert.equals`, `Assert.isTrue`, `Assert.throws` | The same checks with the same failure text. Python, Rust and Ruby write `is_true`; Rust writes `Assert::equals` and PHP `Assert::equals`; Go writes `Assert.Equals`; Java and Groovy write `Assert.throwsError`, because `throws` is a reserved word there. |
| `@MockBean`, `@MockitoBean` | @Fake | A field that the test assigns. Any role that injects it receives it. There is no bean to replace, because the generated constructor already takes the classes that the role needs. |
| `@SpyBean`, `@MockitoSpyBean` | Refused, with the alternative named | There is no bean to wrap. Write Fake and assign the stub (a simple replacement) that the test needs. |
| `@AutoConfigureMockMvc` | Refused, with the alternative named | Call the controller's route method directly. There is no MockMvc. |
| `@TestConfiguration` | @TestSetup | A configuration only for tests, in tests/<Name>TestSetup.<ext>, selected by the sibling unit. |
| `@TestPropertySource` | @TestSettings | At most 64 literal properties of limited size. Each one must be in the realm's own namespace, so a Tac unit cannot reach yon.*. |
| `@ActiveProfiles` | @UseProfiles | Profiles for the unit's context, with the same limits as @WhenProfile. |
| `@DirtiesContext` | @FreshStart | Closes the context between cases. |
| `@Sql` | Seed through the entity adapter | Tachyon never creates or updates a database schema by itself, so there is no script step to attach to. The name is too common to refuse, so the compiler ignores it. |
| `@BeforeEach`, `@Disabled` (JUnit) | A naming convention | These belong to your own test runner, and other libraries may use the same names. So the compiler ignores them. In a @Test unit, a case is an instance method whose name begins with test. JUnit puts its own `@Test` on each case method. Tachyon's @Test marks the test class, so it never goes on a method. A controller route method gets its job from its route annotation, and its name starts with its verb. ty test runs the cases. |
| `@CrossOrigin` | Not supported | Responses carry a fixed set of security headers. You cannot set a cross-origin policy for each endpoint. |
| `@ControllerAdvice`, `@RestControllerAdvice` | @ErrorHandler | A class in server/controllers/<Name>ErrorHandler. Every controller of the same language uses it. The compiler refuses the Spring names and names @ErrorHandler. |
| `@ExceptionHandler` | @HandlesError | Goes on an instance method of an @ErrorHandler class and takes no argument. The declared type of the first parameter is the handled error, like Spring's form without an argument. @ResponseStatus sets its status. An unmatched error still becomes a fixed error response with a correlation identifier (an ID that links the response to the server logs). Internal error details never cross the HTTP boundary. |
| `@EnableAsync` | Not needed | @InBackground marks the listener itself, in the languages whose methods can be asynchronous. |
| `@Scheduled` | @Schedule | Goes on a worker under server/workers, with fixedDelaySeconds and initialDelaySeconds instead of cron and TimeUnit. The .tachyonrc workers object still works. A source uses one or the other. |
| `@EnableScheduling` | Not needed | A worker under server/workers that has a cadence is scheduled. There is no switch to turn the feature on. |

Most differences have one shared cause. Tachyon keeps each annotation small and checks it at compile time. Every annotation above that Tachyon accepts appears earlier on this page, with an example in each language that accepts it.

Members without this: as in a Spring service, Java, Kotlin, C#, Groovy and Dart can read a class field by its name. Swift methods can use the field name too. Keep the receiver when a parameter or local shadows the member; Swift captured closures keep self., and Dart initializing formals keep this. F# private values may use let bindings, while members retain their explicit self identifier. JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Rust, Go, PHP and Lua retain the receivers their language requires. TY1362 is an optional suggestion, off by default, enabled per realm with tac.implicitmembers.suggest or implicitmembers.suggest.
